expectations.text: Classifies the partner need into a shape before choosing a mechanism (stored data, events, live data, or the partner's own capabilities)
expectations.evidence: Section 2 'Classification (workflow step 1)' table: stored data, events pushed into storage, live data.

expectations.text: Identifies tracking number and carrier name as stored data the platform can hold, not data that must be computed live by the partner at query time
expectations.evidence: Table row: 'Tracking number, carrier name | Stored data on Order'.

expectations.text: Identifies parcel status updates as an event-driven need served by webhooks or partner write-back, not a partner resolver
expectations.evidence: 'Status updates as the parcel moves | Events pushed into storage'; partners POST events to /partner/v1/shipments/{id}/events.

expectations.text: Recommends platform-stored, app-owned namespaced extension fields or objects as the default mechanism for the tracking data
expectations.evidence: Recommends a platform-owned canonical `Shipment` type fed by an ingest connector (rung 2). The ranking lists app-owned extension data first on efficiency, but it is not the recommended mechanism, and no namespaced extension fields are proposed.

expectations.text: Explicitly declines to put Quayside's subgraph into the existing first-party production supergraph
expectations.evidence: 'Don't onboard Quayside's subgraph into the supergraph... Refuse it for all three partners.'

expectations.text: Does not produce an onboarding procedure for a partner subgraph into the production supergraph as the main deliverable
expectations.evidence: The main deliverable is the platform-owned Shipment design plus partner ingest API.

expectations.text: Names the condition under which a partner-hosted resolver or partner subgraph would become justified (data that must be live and computed by the partner)
expectations.evidence: Section 7: rung 5 only if 'live entity data a single mediated field can't shape, partners few and under contract, and you can staff partner schema review'.

expectations.text: Ranks the candidate mechanisms with an explicit ordering (e.g. using > or a ranked list), not a flat unranked menu
expectations.evidence: 'Efficiency: app-owned extension data > webhooks plus callback > ingested connector' and the other ranking lines.

expectations.text: Requires a partner namespace or reserved prefix for the partner's extension definitions
expectations.evidence: The main design has no partner extension definitions and no prefix rule. The `Quayside_` namespace appears only in the live-data fallback (rung 3).

expectations.text: States that partner extension data should be visible only to tenants that installed or authorized that partner
expectations.evidence: Says 'There is no installed partner concept because partners never appear in the graph'; visibility is per buyer's own orders, not per installing tenant.

expectations.text: Defines what happens to the partner's definitions and values when a tenant uninstalls or the partner leaves
expectations.evidence: 'Offboard: revoke the credential. Shipment data stays in your storage, and no graph field disappears.'

expectations.text: Uses the January peak deadline as a reason favouring the mechanisms that need no partner engineering
expectations.evidence: 'The January date (interview answer 7) moves nothing. It only promotes rung 3 for live data, and this need is stored.'
